_meta.description: Wallets of Indian exchanges and Indian-run platforms, each row with the public source that names it. Every row is also in that chain's exchange label file (config.Chain.labels_path) as {exchange, label, type}, which is what the matcher reads; this file records where each came from.
_meta.provenance: Public sources only, read without an API key on 14 Nov 2026. (1) The explorer's own public name tag on the address page (etherscan.io/address/<a>, polygonscan.com/address/<a>), read from the page title; source_date is the page's own 'As at' time. Candidate addresses to look up came from dawsbot/eth-labels @ 14247ba8cf4686b747938248bee34c66089fa9d9 (data/csv/accounts.csv) and brianleect/etherscan-labels @ 923aba72c7e2d0682f7ae6194b6140bd90668dc9 (data/*/combined/combinedAllLabels.json); a candidate became a row only if the explorer page for that chain carries the tag. (2) CoinSwitch's own lists of its major (custodial) wallets, published on its blog on 6 Jan 2023 and refreshed on 27 Jul 2023; the chain is the explorer each address links to.
_meta.not_done: No ownership was inferred: no clustering and no guessing. A Polygon row carries the tag PolygonScan itself shows on that address's Polygon page (Etherscan-family explorers show an address's public name tag on each chain they serve), and only where that page shows Polygon transactions. Pages behind a bot check (bscscan.com, arbiscan.io, Etherscan's label lists, the CoinDCX and ZebPay proof-of-reserves pages) were not read; nothing was done to get past one.
_meta.activity: Every Ethereum and Polygon row's address page showed at least one transaction on that chain (EOA or contract as the page says; a contract is typed contract_wallet). The BSC row was checked on the public BNB Chain RPC (bsc-dataseed.bnbchain.org: no code, nonce 210) and the Tron row on TronGrid without a key (account created 2022-12-27, last active 2025-05-26), both on 2026-11-14.
_meta.kinds: type is the matcher's wallet type; kind is what the source says the wallet is.
_meta.checked: Each address passes the chain's validator (EIP-55 checksum on the spelling a source published, Base58Check on Tron), appears once, and is on no sanctions, freeze, threat, gambling, router or never-flag token list.
_meta.schema: rows: [{address, chain, exchange, label, type, kind, source, source_date, retrieved_on, published_as?}]
